REFERENCE BY THE CHAIR
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, today, the 22nd of March, is World Water 
Day, a day celebrated every year to focus attention on the importance of water. 
This year, the day is dedicated to the theme 'Nature for Water' which accentuates 
the need for exploring nature-based solutions to overcome the water challenges being 
faced in the 21st century.
The theme is relevant for our country where climatic change, population growth 
and changing consumption patterns are contaminating our fresh water systems and 
depleting ground water tables at an alarming trend.
The day serves as a unique occasion to work together to protect our ecosystem 
and alter our lifestyles in concordance with nature, to preserve water. The day also 
focuses on advocating efficient water management and water sharing practices. Reduce, 
reuse and recycle water for a liveable planet.
I hope the entire House will join me in supporting the conservation of fresh 
water resources through natural methods to ensure availability of sufficient potable 
water for our future generations. Thank you.

(a)	 whether	 it	 is	 a	 fact	 that	 human	 trafficking	 is	 taking	 place	 on	 a	 large	 scale	
from the remote forest and tribal areas of Jharkhand namely, Khunti, Dumka, Simdega, 
Gumla, Ranchi, Chaibasa, Lohardaga and Palamu;
(b) whether it is also a fact that touts play an important role in well planned 
human	 trafficking;

(c) whether the Central and State Government have prepared a list of touts on 
the basis of intense surveillance; and
(d)	 if	 so,	 by	 when	 strict	 action	 would	 be	 taken	 and	 human	 trafficking	 would	
be stopped?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR): (a) to (d) The Government of Jharkhand 
has	 informed	 that	 complaints	 are	 received	 from	 time	 to	 time	 pertaining	 to	 trafficking	
of girls in the garb of providing employment. It has been reported that touts play a 
role in such cases. Several districts of Jharkhand have prepared lists of such touts 
and surveillance is being maintained by the Government of Jharkhand. List of such 
touts is not maintained centrally. 
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India. The responsibility to maintain law and order and protection 
of citizens primarily rests with respective State Governments. State Governments 
are competent to deal with such offences under extant provisions of law. However, 
the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has been supplementing the efforts of States 
and UTs by providing them regular guidance through various advisories issued on 
human	 trafficking	 from	 time	 to	 time.	 These	 advisories	 are	 available	 on	 the	 website	
of Ministry of Home Affairs at: http://mha.gov.in. 
The	 Ministry	 of	 Home	 Affairs	 has	 provided	 financial	 assistance	 to	 States	 to	 set	
up	Anti	 Human	 Trafficking	Units	 to	 curb	 human	 trafficking	cases.	 MHA	 also	 engages	
with	 Nodal	 Officers	 of	 Anti	 Human	 Trafficking	 Units	 of	 States	 from	 time	 to	 time	
and	 provides	 guidance	 in	 handling	 human	 trafficking	 issues.	
Financial assistance is also provided by MHA to Judicial Academies and States 
for holding ‘Judicial Colloquiums’ and ‘State level Conferences’ which are aimed at 
sensitizing	 the	 judicial	 officers	 about	 various	 provisions	 of	 law	 relevant	 to	 trafficking	
and	 in	 sensitizing	 law	 enforcement	 officials	 about	 their	 duties	 and	 role	 in	 curbing	
trafficking	 in	 close	 coordination	 with	 civil	 society	 organisations	 and	 border	 guarding	
forces. 
MHA also advises the Ministry of Women and Child Development and the 
Ministry	 of	 Labour	 and	 Employment	 for	 rehabilitation	 of	 victims	 of	 trafficking,	 and	
to keep a watch on fraudulent placement agencies in States which dupe unscrupulous 
victims in the name of providing employment. Ministry of Railways has also been 
addressed by MHA to alert GRP and other railway staff to keep a close vigil on 
any suspicious activity of women and children being transported through Railways 
for	 the	 purpose	 of	 trafficking.

Development of traditional and tribal sports
*273. SHRI MD. NADIMUL HAQUE: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) what steps have been taken by Government with regard to travel facilities 
in order to facilitate people to reach the proposed site of National Sports University 
in Manipur, the details thereof;
(b) what steps have been taken by Government for promotion of traditional and 
tribal sports, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government considers inclusion of the local and tribal communities 
in development of traditional and tribal sports, respectively, if so, the steps taken 
thereon?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (COL. RAJYA V ARDHAN SINGH RATHORE): (a) Sir, Imphal, where 
National Sports University is being set up, has road and air connectivity. Imphal 
Airport is connected by Air India and other private commercial airlines. National 
Sports University from Imphal Airport can be reached by local transport.
Further, nearest Railway Station from Imphal is at Dimapur (Nagaland) which is 
at a distance of about 200 KM from Imphal. Imphal is well connected with Dimapur 
by road. People can reach Imphal from Dimapur by bus/local transport.
(b) and (c)  Sports being a State subject, promotion and development of traditional 
and tribal sports in the country is primarily the responsibility of the concerned State 
Governments and National Sports Federations (NSFs).
In order to complement/supplement the efforts of the State Governments and 
NSFs, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has been implementing various 
schemes for promotion of sports including traditional and tribal sports in the country.
Traditional and tribal sports form an integral part of the culture and life style of 
local and tribal communities and the Government considers that active co-operation 
and support of local and tribal communities is essential for successful promotion and 
development of traditional and tribal sports.
The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is implementing the Khelo India Scheme, 
which inter alia has a vertical of “Promotion of rural and indigenous/tribal games”. 
In order to showcase our rural and indigenous/tribal games, annual competitions will 
be held annually under the Scheme in rural and indigenous/tribal games alternately. 
A dynamic and interactive website providing information on such games will also 

Written Ans. to Std. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 19
be put up for disseminating information as well as encouraging children and youth 
to take up these games in a major way, paving way for their future mainstreaming.
Further, to preserve and promote traditional sports in the country, Sports Authority 
of India under its National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC) Scheme has introduced 
a sub-scheme whereby schools engaged in the promotion of Indigenous Games and 
Martial Arts (IGMA) are adopted and provided with facilities for the promotion of 
identified	 Indigenous	 Games	 and	 Martial	 Arts.	 Sports	 Authority	 of	 India	 (SAI)	 has	
adopted 10 IGMA schools across the country to identify talented sportspersons in 9 
Indigenous Games and Martial Arts, and selected trainees are provided with training 
facilities in the form of expert coach, sports kit, insurance, stipend, annual grant to the 
school for procurement of equipment, scouting of talent and to conduct competitions.
Presently, under IGMA Scheme, total 164 trainees (90 boys and 74 girls) are 
being trained in 10 IGMA Centres across the country.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR): (a) to (c) In order to 
improve livelihood of the unorganised workers in the Country, including in the urban 
areas, the Government has taken various steps by way of encouraging private sector, 
fast tracking various projects involving substantial investment and increasing public 
expenditure on schemes like Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme 
(PMEGP) and providing skills to enhance their income earning capacity.
A Scheme called “Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana” (PMRPY) has been 
launched by the Government in the year 2016-17. Under this scheme, employers are 
provided an incentive where the Government is paying the employer’s contribution 
of 8.33% EPS made to new employees. In textiles (apparel and made-ups) sector, 
the Government is also paying the 3.67% EPF contribution of employers in addition 
to paying the 8.33% EPS contribution. This scheme not only helps in employment 
creation but also helps formalization of informal jobs.
The Government is implementing the National Career Service Project (NCSP) 
using technology to bring more employment opportunities to jobseekers and matching 
the job requirement with the skills sets available to these workers.
“Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY- 
NULM)” is being implemented to reduce poverty and vulnerability of urban poor 
households. Self-employment Programme is one of the vital components of the Mission.
The Government is also encouraging labor-intensive manufacturing, promoting 
tourism and agro-based industries. Besides, the Make in India, Digital India, Skill 
India Schemes are being implemented by the Government for this purpose.
MUDRA and START UPS schemes have been initiated by the Government for 
facilitating self-employment. Loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)

 SHRI NEERAJ SHEKHAR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has agreed under pressure from the World Trade

below 10 per cent of gross agricultural production;

farmers and food security of the country; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY): (a) No, Sir.
(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above.
(c) The relevant rules of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) categorise all 
agricultural support measures broadly into those that distort trade and those that 
have no or minimal trade-distorting effect. There are limits on the amount of trade-
distorting support that can be provided. Agricultural support measures that have no 
or minimal trade-distorting effect can be freely used. The rules applicable to most 
developing	 countries	 allow	 for	 product-specific	trade	 distorting	 support	 upto	 10%	 (‘de 
minimis’) of the value of production of the product. Similarly, total trade-distorting 
support,	 which	 is	 not	 specific	 to	 any	 product,	 can	 be	 provided	 upto	 a	 limit	 of	 10%	
of the total value of agricultural production. India has always kept its trade-distorting 
support within the applicable limits. Further, India has been providing input subsidies 
and non- trade-distorting agricultural support, where the limits do not apply.

Usual Principal Status (UPS) Approach
Under the Usual Principal Status (UPS) approach, the major time criterion based 
on the 365 days is used to determine the activity pursued by a person. Accordingly, 
the major time spent by a person (183 days or more) is used to determine whether 
the person is in the labour force or out of labour force. A person found unemployed 
under	 this	 approach	 reflects	 the	 chronic	 unemployment.	 In	 the	 present	 survey,	 the	

50 Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [RAJYA SABHA] ...for the 21st March, 2018
Usual Principal Status approach estimates are derived for a moving reference period 
of last twelve months. 
Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status (UPSS) Approach
Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status (UPSS) Approach is a hybrid one which 
takes into consideration both the major time criterion and shorter time period  
(30 days or more in any economic activity). Thus, a person who has worked even 
for 30 days or more in any economic activity during the reference period of last 
twelve months is considered as employed under this approach. In this approach, the 
reference period is same as taken in the Usual Principal Status approach (UPS).

Deriving advantages from the impacts of WTO policies
2888. SHRI MANISH GUPTA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether India has been able to derive any decisive advantages from the 
impacts of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) policies, if so, the details thereof; 
and
(b)	 whether	 there	 is	 any	 serious	conflict	in	 the	WTO	between	rich	 and	 developing	
countries in respect of retention of subsidies and resisting opening of the markets 
of the former; if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY): (a) The WTO rules have been framed and 
adopted through a process of consensus. India, like many other developing countries, 
joined the consensus after ensuring that its trade interests would be protected. The 
trade rules of the WTO, its dispute settlement mechanism and methods of decision-
making provide stability and predictability to the global trading system. As a developing 
country,	 India	 has	 been	 able	 to	 get	 the	 benefit	 of	 various	 special	 and	 differential	
treatment provisions in the WTO Agreements. These special provisions include, for 
example, longer time periods for implementing Agreements and commitments or 
measures to increase trading opportunities for developing countries. The opening in 
the global markets has helped Indian trade both in goods and services.
(b) There are differences in the positions of the developed and developing countries 
on various issues under negotiation in the WTO. For example, in the agriculture 
negotiations, while developed countries are now focusing on gaining more market 
access for their exports, developing countries have been calling for the elimination 
of the large agricultural subsidies provided by developed countries, which was one 
of the key objectives of the negotiations. Further, exports from developing countries 
also face various non-tariff barriers in developed country markets.

WTO's agenda for resource poor farming families
2889. SHRI MANISH GUPTA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the World Trade Organisation (WTO) has any visible agenda for 
the resource-poor farming families;
(b) whether the WTO Agreement requires India to pay more attention to quality, 
value addition and the sustainability aspects of its agriculture, if so, the details thereof; 
and
(c) whether there is a mismatch between production and post-harvest technologies 
and lack of infrastructure for handling perishable commodities affecting India's exports?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY): (a) Special and differential treatment 
provisions are available for developing countries across the agreements of the World 
Trade Organization (WTO), which, inter alia, are intended to safeguard the interests 
of low income or resource-poor farmers in developing countries. In terms of the 
provisions of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, input and investment subsidies can 
be provided without any limit to low-income, resource-poor farmers in developing 
countries.
(b) The WTO rules regarding sanitary and phytosanitary measures allow countries 
to adopt or enforce measures necessary to protect human, animal and plant life or 
health subject to the requirement that these measures are not applied in a manner 
which	 would	 constitute	 a	 means	 of	 arbitrary	 or	 unjustifiable	 discrimination	 between	
WTO members or a disguised restriction on international trade. Such provisions 
encourage WTO members to improve their farming methods and the manner in 
which they use various inputs such as chemicals and pesticides.
(c) Exports of agricultural products depend on a number of factors including the 
availability and quality of production and post-harvest technology and infrastructure. 
All such factors are taken into account while framing agricultural trade policy.

Fall in export of honey
2899. DR. KANWAR DEEP SINGH: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the export of honey is expected to fall;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and its effect on producers thereof; and
(c) the steps being taken to tackle this situation?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY): (a) and (b) The details of India’s  
export of Natural Honey, during the last three years and the current year, are as 
under:–
Quantity	 in	 MT;	 V alue	in	 US	 $	 Million
2014-15 2015-16 2016-17 2017-18 
(April-December)
Quantity Value Quantity Value Quantity Value Quantity Value
29578.56 87.40 38177.04 108.68 45055.45 83.32 36348.57 73.98
Source: DGCI&S.
During 2016-17, while the exports increased in quantity terms, there was a decline 
in the value terms. This can be attributed to fall in international prices, which crashed 
from around USD 3000/MT in 2015-16 to around USD 1800/MT in 2016-17. The 
prices have increased only marginally during the current year.
(c) The promotion of exports of agricultural commodities like honey is a 
continuous process. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development 
Authority (APEDA), an autonomous organisation under the administrative control of 
the Department of Commerce, has the mandate to promote exports of agricultural 
and processed food products, including honey. APEDA provides assistance to the 
exporters of agricultural and processed food products, including honey, under various 
component of its scheme “Agriculture and Processed Food Export promotion Scheme 
of APEDA” viz. Infrastructure Development, Quality Development and Market

pending in the country during the last three years; and

‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India. The responsibility to maintain law and order, protection of life 
and property of the citizens rests primarily with the respective State Governments. 
The State Governments are competent to deal with such offences under the extant 
provisions of laws. 
The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which has come into force since 
3rd February, 2013 on crime against women, has enhanced punishment for crimes 
such as rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism, acid attacks, indecent gestures 
such as words and inappropriate touch etc. The new law has provisions for increased 
sentence for rape convicts, including life-term and death sentence, besides providing 
for stringent punishment for offences such as acid attacks, stalking and voyeurism.
Ministry of Home Affairs has issued Advisories for combating crimes against 
women. These Advisories are also available on www.mha.gov.in.

India (OCI) applications in Britain during last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons for pending OCI applications; and
(d) the details of the plan to give the OCI Card on the pending applications?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

Occupancy rate in jails
2933. SHRI TIRUCHI SIV A: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased 
to state:
(a) the number and names of jails where the occupancy rate is more than 100 
per cent; and
(b) Government's plan to urgently reduce overcrowding in these jails?

130 Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [RAJYA SABHA] ...for the 21st March, 2018
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR): (a) State/UT-wise details of jails where the 
occupancy rate is more than 100 per cent are given in the Statement (See below). 
(b) ‘Prisons’ is a State subject as per entry 4 of List II of the Seventh Schedule 
to the Constitution of India. The administration and management of prisons is primarily 
the responsibility of respective State Governments. However, the Government of India 
has been providing regular guidance to State Governments in prison management 
through various advisories issued from time to time. 
The Government of India has taken various administrative and legislatives 
measures for reducing overcrowding in prisons. Some of the initiatives taken are: 
(i) Establishment of Fast Track Courts (FTCs), (ii) Creation of additional capacity 
of prisons through the scheme of Modernization of Prisons, (iii) Launch of National 
Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms etc. 
Introduction of the concept of plea bargaining through Section 265 of Cr. PC 
and insertion of a new Section viz. 436-A in Cr. PC on the maximum period for 
which an undertrial prisoner can be detained, are some other special initiatives taken 
by the Government of India to reduce overcrowding in jails.
Besides the advisories issued from time to time, Model Prison Manual 2016 was 
also forwarded by the Ministry of Home Affairs to all States and Union Territories 
in May, 2016. The Prison Manual has a dedicated chapter on ‘Undertrial Prisoners’, 
which provides guidance on the facilities to be provided to undertrials viz. legal 
defence, interview with lawyers, signing of Vakalatnama, application to Courts for 
legal aid at Government cost etc.
The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) has also been providing free 
legal services to all under trial prisoners through its legal service clinics running in 
jails all over India. NALSA is also promoting plea bargaining for quick disposal 
of cases falling within the parameters spelt out in the provisions of plea bargaining 
given in Code of Criminal Procedure. All these measures are intended to help the 
States and UTs to address the issue of overcrowding in prisons.

India's crime statistics
2937. SHRIMATI VIJILA SATHYANANTH: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state :
(a) whether it is a fact that India's crime statistics presented by National Crime 
Records Bureau (NCRB) is deceptive;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c)	 whether	 it	 is	 also	 a	 fact	 that	 old	 and	 wrong	 population	 figures,	 misleading	
classifications	 distort	 the	 results;	 and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR): (a) and (b) No, Sir. NCRB published the 
first	 report	 of	 ‘Crime	 in	 India’	 for	 the	 year	 1983	 and	 the	 methodology	 for	 crime	
statistics since then has not been changed by NCRB. NCRB collects Annual data 
on cognizable crime as registered by the Police Departments of the States/UTs in 
prescribed proformae. NCRB then compiles the data furnished by the States/UTs and 
publishes the same in the form of a report.
(c)	 and	 (d)	 NCRB	 takes	 population	 figures	 as	 released	 by	 the	 Registrar	 General	
of India (RGI) on the basis of 2001 census projected up to 2026. The population 
projections of 2016 based on 2011 census, have not been released as yet, by RGI.

Acid attacks on girls/women
2939. SHRIMATI SASIKALA PUSHPA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the fact that incidents of acid attacks on 
girls/women has not reduced in spite of the curbs imposed by Government in the

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 137
(b) if so, the details of acid attacks during past three years;
(c) whether Government will come forward to prescribe stringent punishment of 
life imprisonment to both retail acid seller and its purchaser, who are two important 
links in acid attack incidents, in which victims are girls who incur heavy expenditure 
on recovery;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR): (a) to (e) As per the information provided by 
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), the details of State/UT-wise cases registered, 
cases charge-sheeted, cases convicted, persons arrested, persons charge-sheeted and 
cases resulted in conviction for acid attack (Section 326A IPC) and attempt to acid 
attack (Section 326B IPC) for crime against women are given in the Statement-I 
and II (See below) respectively.
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India. The responsibility to maintain law and order, protection of life 
and property of the citizens rests primarily with the respective State Governments. 
The State Governments are competent to deal with such offences under the extant 
provisions of laws. 
Criminal Amendment Act 2013 came in to force w.e.f. 03.02.2013 wherein 326A 
and 326B have been inserted which penalise the act of intentionally causing damage 
to the body of a person, or burning or maiming a person by throwing acid with 
imprisonment for minimum of 10 years that may extend up to life imprisonment 
and	 with	 fine.	 It	 also	 penalises	 the	 attempt	 to	 cause	 harm	 by	 throwing	 acid	 with	
minimum	 of	 five	 and	 maximum	 of	 seven	 years	 of	 imprisonment.	
Ministry of Home Affairs has issued advisories dated 30th August, 2013 on 
measures to be taken to prevent acid attacks on people and for treatment and 
rehabilitation of survivors and another advisory dated 20th April, 2015 on expediting 
cases of acid attack on women which are available at www.mha.gov.in. However, 
there is no proposal under consideration for prescribing stringent punishment of life 
imprisonment to both retail acid seller and its purchaser.

Policy of granting medical visas
2940. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state :
(a) whether it is a fact that Government has imposed a condition that medical 
visa request by Pakistani nationals need authentication of Pakistani Foreign Ministry;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is present policy of granting medical visas to foreign nationals; and
(d) how many foreign nationals were granted medical visas during last two 
years, country-wise?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU): (a) and (b) As per procedure adopted by the High Commission 
of India (HCI), Islamabad, in cases of medical visas involving organ transplants 
only (usually liver and kidney) the HCI requires authentication by the Ministry of 
Foreign Affairs of Pakistan. The authentication is in the form of Ministry of Foreign 
Affair's	 stamp	 on	 the	 affidavit	 submitted	 by	 the	 organ	 donor	 informing	 that	 he/she	
is donating his/her organ on his/her own volition.
(c) The present policy of granting medical visas to Pakistani nationals is given 
in the Statement-I (See below).
(d) Country-wise details of foreign nationals who were granted medical visas 
during the last two years (2016 and 2017) are given in the Statement-II. 

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 147
Statement-I
The present policy of granting medical visas to Pakistani nationals:–
(i) A single entry Medical visa may be granted to Pakistani nationals whose sole 
purpose is to seek medical treatment in established/ recognized/ specialized 
hospitals/ treatment centers in India and who have obtained prior appointment 
for	 medical	 treatment.	 The	 Visa	 may	 be	 granted	 after	 due	 verification	 of	
documents by the Mission.
(ii)	 The	 Visa	 issuing	 officer	 shall	 satisfy	 himself/herself	 about	 the	 bonafides	 and	
the need of the foreign national to come to India for medical treatment. 
Although not exhaustive, the following illustrative list of ailments would 
be considered for grant of medical visa: serious ailments requiring neuro-
surgery; ophthalmic disorders; heart-related problems; renal disorders; organ 
transplantation; congenital disorders; gene-therapy; radio-therapy; cancer related 
problems; plastic surgery; joint replacement etc.
(iii) The initial period of validity for such a visa may be upto a period of 
three months, or the period of treatment, whichever is less, which can be 
extended by the Ministry of Home Affairs on the recommendation of the 
State Governments/FRRO supported by appropriate medical documents.
(iv) The patient coming to India for medical treatment may be permitted one 
attendant who may be granted medical attendant visa (Med X) visa co-
terminus with the ‘Med visa’ of the patient.
(v) Pakistan nationals holding a Medical Visa will be required to register 
themselves with the FRRO/FRO concerned within 7 days of arrival in India, 
irrespective of the duration of the visa. Pakistan nationals holding a Medical 
Attendant Visa will be required to register themselves with the FRRO/FRO 
concerned within 24 hours of arrival in India, irrespective of the duration 
of the visa.
(vi) The patients who have obtained prior appointment with reputed Doctor(s)/
Clinic(s)/Hospital(s) in Punjab may be granted visa for medical treatment 
after	 due	 verification	 of	 documents	 by	 the	 HCI,	 Islamabad.	 Apart	 from	
the applicant, visa may also be given to one blood relation/dependant as 
Attendant.

Overcrowding in jails
2944. DR. R. LAKSHMANAN: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the fact that all the jails across the country 
are overcrowded and the number of inmates in jails are beyond the sanctioned 
strength; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government has formulated any scheme to solve the problem of 
overcrowding in Indian jails and to achieve the prescribed international occupancy 
rate for jail inmates; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR): (a) to (d) State/UT wise details of total 
number of jails across the country, its capacity, inmate population, and occupancy 
rate, as on 31.12.2016, as compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau, are 
given in the Statement (See below).
Prisons is a State subject under Entry 4 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution of India and administration and management of prisons is primarily 
the responsibility of respective State Governments. However, the Ministry of Home 
Affairs has been providing regular guidance to States and UTs through various 
advisories issued from time to time and also through the Model Prison Manual 2016 
to reduce overcrowding in Prisons by adopting various ways and means.
The Government of India has taken various administrative and legislatives 
measures for reducing overcrowding in prisons. Some of the initiatives taken are: 
(i) Establishment of Fast Track Courts (FTCs), (ii) Creation of additional capacity 
of prisons through the scheme of Modernization of Prisons, (iii) Launch of National 
Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms etc. 
Introduction of the concept of plea bargaining through Section 265 of Cr PC and 
insertion of a new Section viz. 436-A in Cr PC on the maximum period for which 
an under trial prisoner can be detained are some of the special initiatives taken by 
the Government of India to reduce overcrowding in jails.

156 Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [RAJYA SABHA] ...for the 21st March, 2018
The Model Prison Manual 2016 has a dedicated chapter on ‘Undertrial Prisoners’, 
which provides guidance on the facilities to be provided to undertrials viz. legal 
defence, interview with lawyers, signing of Vakalatnama, application to Courts for 
legal aid at Government cost etc. These measures are also focused at reducing 
overcrowding in prisons.
The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) has also been providing free 
legal services to all under trial prisoners through its legal service clinics running in 
jails all over India. NALSA is also promoting plea bargaining for quick disposal 
of cases falling within the parameters spelt out in the provisions of plea bargaining 
given in Code of Criminal Procedure. All these measures are intended to help the 
States and UTs to address the issue of overcrowding in prisons. 
The Ministry of Home Affairs has also taken up the proposal of establishing 
open prisons in States and UTs. Establishment of such open institutions will also 
prove useful in reducing overcrowding in jails.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has also shared the Nelson Mandela Rules – United 
Nations Standard Minimum Rules for treatment of prisoners – with all States and 
UTs and have advised them to follow the guidance provided therein.

2963. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state:

(BGB) have signed an agreement in this regard; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU): (a) to (d) As per an agreement between the Government 
of India and the Government of Bangladesh no defence construction can be raised 
within 150 yards of the either side of International Border (IB) between India

fence will come entirely inside the fencing.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR): (a) to (c) As per data submitted by Bureau 
of Police Research and Development (BPR&D), as on 01.01.2017, the actual strength

police hierarchy from Deputy Inspector General (DIG) and above level, 6.5 per cent 
of the positions have been occupied by women. 
As, ‘Police’ is a State subject falling in List-II of seventh schedule of the 
Constitution of India, it is primarily the responsibility of the State Governments/UTs 
to increase women personnel in police forces to enforce gender equality in policing. 
The Central Government advises the States/UTs from time to time. Accordingly, 
Ministry of Home Affairs has issued advisories dated 22.4.2013, 21.5.2014 and

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 

192 Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [RAJYA SABHA] ...for the 21st March, 2018
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR): (a) The number of 
workers suffering from Asbestosis and the number of Asbestosis cases reported in 
the registered factories under the Factories Act, 1948 reported by Chief Inspector of 
Factories for the last three years is given in the Statement (See below).
(b) The Government of India has enacted the Factories Act, 1948 to ensure 
the safety and health of workers working in the factories registered under the Act. 
The State Governments are empowered under the Act to frame their respective State 
Factories Rules and both the Act and the Rules framed thereunder are enforced by 
the respective State Governments through their State Factories Inspectorate/Directorate 
to ensure the safety and health of the workers working in the registered factories 
including asbestos processing industries.
As per the provisions contained under Section 2(cb) of the Factories Act, 1948 
the "Manufacture, handling and processing of Asbestos and its products" is declared 
as a hazardous process and the same is listed in the First Schedule of the Act and 
accordingly provisions of Chapter IV-A of the Act relating to hazardous processes 
are	 applicable	 to	 such	 factories.	 The	 permissible	 levels	 of	 asbestos	 fibre	 in	 work	
environment are given in Second Schedule of the said Act.
Further, under Section 87 concerning dangerous operations, the State Governments 
are empowered under the Act to declare dangerous operations under the Rules 
where the State Government is of the opinion that any manufacturing process or 
operation carried on in a factory exposes any persons employed in it to a serious 
risk of bodily injury poisoning or disease. Accordingly, the State Governments are 
empowered to frame the rules applicable to any factory or class or description of 
factories under Section 87 of the Factories Act, 1948 and notify the schedule on 
handling and processing of asbestos, manufacture of any article of asbestos and any 
other process of manufacture or otherwise in which asbestos is used in any form. 
Further, in case of violations of any provisions by the occupier or manager of the 
registered factories, prosecutions are launched under Section 92 and 96A of the Act.
(c) Section 7A of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that every occupier shall 
ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare of all workers 
while they are at work in the factory registered under the Factories Act, 1948. 
Further, Section 89 of the Factories Act, 1948 prescribes that where any worker in a 
factory	 registered	 under	 the	 Act	 contracts	 any	 notifiable	 disease	 including	 Asbestosis	
specified	under	 the	Act,	 the	 manager	 of	 the	 factory	 shall	 report	 the	 same	 to	 the	 Chief	
Inspector of Factories and other authorities in their State Factories Rules which is 
enforced by the State Governments who are empowered under the Act to initiate 
penal action under Section 92 of the Act for violation of any of the provision of 
the Act and the Rules framed thereunder.

2974. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN:
 SHRI ANUBHA V MOHANTY:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Labour Bureau's Quarterly Survey for the period April-June, 2017 
has shown an increase of 64,000 jobs across eight leading sectors and also 87,000 
jobs lost in the manufacturing sector during the same quarter;
(b) whether this is an indication that the 'Make in India' project being PM's pet 
project has proved to be 'damp squib', despite all efforts pushed by Government to 
make it a success; and
(c) whether most of jobs were created in Education and Health sectors since 
April, 2016, whereas the manufacturing sector showed a reverse trend by losing jobs 
severely affecting the 'Make in India' project?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTERY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR): (a) Yes, Sir. Labour 
Bureau’s revamped Quarterly Employment Survey (QES) launched in April, 2016 
measures relative change in employment situation over successive quarters in sizeable 
segment of Non-farm Industrial economy. The survey covers eight major sectors which 
constitute around 81 percent of the total employment of establishments employing 
10 or more workers as per the 6th Economic census, conducted during January, 
2013 to April, 2014. The Sixth QES has shown an increase of 64,000 jobs during 
the April- June quarter of 2017. This increasing trend is observed over and above 
the increasing trend in four preceeding quarters. The results also indicate a fall in 
manufacturing sector employment to the tune of 87,000. This is attributed to seasonal 
activities during this period since unit level data suggest that fall in employment 
was essentially registered in brick manufacturing units with the onset of monsoons.

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 195
(b) No, Sir. Survey does not capture the employment data from new units which 
emerged after the 6th Economic Census i.e. 2013-14.
(c) Yes, Sir. The 6th round of QES results show that most of the jobs in 
the April – June 2017 quarter have been created in Education and Health Sectors. 
However, in this round there is a decrease in manufacturing sector, the reasons for

2978. SHRI TIRUCHI SIV A: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
be pleased to state:
(a)	 whether	 the	 Consumer	 Confidence	 Survey	 (CSS)	 by	 the	 RBI	 stated	 that	 the	
people are beginning to realize themselves that the Indian economy is not creating 
jobs;
(b) what is the Government doing for creating more jobs in the labour intensive 
sectors; and
(c) by when is Government planning to reform the labour laws so that the 
legislative compliance for industrial units is reduced?

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 201
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR): (a) The Reserve Bank 
released	 the	 latest	 results	 of	 the	 December,	 2017	 round	 of	 the	 Consumer	 Confidence	
Survey (CCS). The survey was conducted in six metropolitan cities - Bengaluru; 
Chennai; Hyderabad; Kolkata; Mumbai; and New Delhi and obtained 5,035 responses 
on households’ perceptions and expectations on the general economic situation, the 
employment scenario, the overall price situation and their own income and spending. 
In the highlights of the report, the households’ current perceptions on the general 
economic	 situation	 improved	 and	 edged	 up	 towards	 the	 neutral	 level	 after	 five	quarters	
of pessimism; their one year ahead outlook improved further within positive terrain. 
Further, the employment situation continued to be a major concern, but the current 
sentiment was less pessimistic than in the two previous rounds while the outlook 
strengthened.
(b) Government has taken various steps for generating employment in the country 
like encouraging private sector of economy, fast tracking various projects involving 
substantial investment and increasing public expenditure on schemes like Prime 
Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), Mahatma Gandhi National 
Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA), Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya 
Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) and Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National 
Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM). The Make in India, Skill India, Digital 
India schemes are being implemented by the Government and these are likely to 
enhance the employment base. MUDRA and START UPS scheme are initiated by 
the Government for facilitating self employment.
Government has decided to strategically promote labour-intensive manufacturing 
and expand employment opportunities by promoting tourism and agro-based industries.
A Scheme called “Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana” has been initiated 
by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in the year 2016-17 for incentivising 
industry for promoting employment generation. Under this scheme employers would 
be provided an incentive to enhance employment where the Government will pay the 
employer’s contribution of 8.33% EPS made to new employees. In textiles (apparel 
and made-ups) sector, the Government will also pay the 3.67% EPF contribution of 
employers in addition. Government has also announced a booster package of ` 6000 
crores for the textile sector which is an employment intensive sector.
(c) Reforms in labour laws are an ongoing process to update the legislative 
system	 to	 address	 the	 need	 of	 the	 hour	 so	 as	 to	 make	 them	 more	 effective,	 flexible	
and in sync with emerging economic and industrial scenario. The Second National 
Commission on Labour has recommended that the existing Labour Laws should be 

202 Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [RAJYA SABHA] ...for the 21st March, 2018
broadly	 grouped	 into	 four	 or	 five	 Labour	 Codes	 on	 functional	 basis.	 Accordingly,	
the Ministry has taken steps for drafting four Labour Codes on Wages; Industrial 
Relations; Social Security and Welfare; and Occupation Safety, Health and Working 
Conditions, by simplifying, amalgamating and rationalizing the relevant provisions 
of the existing Central Labour Laws. Out of these, the Labour Code on Wages 
has been introduced in Lok Sabha on 10.08.2017 and subsequently, referred to the 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Labour. The rest of the codes are at pre- 
legislative consultative stage. The process of Legislative reforms on Labour includes 
consultation with stakeholders including Central Trade Unions, Employers’ Association 
and State Governments in the form of tripartite consultation. Suggestions/comments 
received during the tripartite consultations are taken into account/considered while 
finalizing	 the	 amendment	 in	 various	 Act/Rules.

FICCI-NASSCOM study on changing job roles of Indian workforce
2985. SHRI SAMBHAJI CHHATRAPATI: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken note of the study conducted by Federation 
of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) - The National Association 
of Software and Services Companies (NASSCOM) concluding that 37 per cent of 
Indian workforce would be employed in new job roles by 2022;
(b) if so, the details thereof and reaction of Government on the study; and
(c) whether Government has any plan to constitute a panel of experts to study 
the	 findings	 and	 make	 recommendations	 for	 preparedness?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR): (a) to (c) FICCI- 
NASSCOM report on "Future of Jobs in India - A 2022 perspective" is the empirical 
based study which examines the global megatrends and its impact on Indian economy. 
The report also covers an in depth analysis of impact of technology, demography 
and	 globalization	 in	 five	 crucial	 sectors	 -	 automotive,	 textiles	 and	 apparel,	 BFSI,	 IT-	
BPM and retail. It also assesses and highlights the changing nature of jobs in these 
sectors, skill requirements and policy recommendations. The report highlighted that 
by 2022, 9% would be deployed in new jobs that do not exist today, 37% would 
be in jobs that have radically changed skill sets. All the new forms of employment 
are	 expected	 to	 add	 a	 further	 20%–25%	 to	 the	 workforce	 of	 the	 current	 defined	
"organized" sector in 2022. This would increase the share of the organized sector in 
the overall economy to 10% from current level of 8%, i.e. approximately 60 million 
in a workforce of 600 million.

3013. SHRI SAMBHAJI CHHATRAPATI: Will the Minister of SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any plan to empower informal economy through

AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP (SHRI ANANTKUMAR HEGDE): (a) to (d) Presently, 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been implementing 
Pradhan Mantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan (PM-YUV A). The scheme aims to create 
an enabling ecosystem for Entrepreneurship Development through entrepreneurship 
education and training across the country in select Institutes of Higher Learning 
(Universities, Colleges and Premier Institutes), schools, Industrial Training Centers 
(ITIs) and Entrepreneurship Development Centres (EDCs) for over a period of 
five	 years	 (2017-18	 to	 2021-22).	 Additionally,	 students	 will	 get	 easy	 access	 to	 a	
robust network of peers, mentors incubators, funds and business services through 
an online platform. Under the PM YUV A scheme, interested students will be given 
entrepreneurship education and training, including social entrepreneurship. So far, 
239 Institutes of Higher Learning have been empanelled to impart entrepreneurship 
education throughout the country and entrepreneurship courses have started in 226 
Institutes of Higher Learning. Keeping in view the mandate of MSDE, an end to end 
customized entrepreneurship orientation module has been integrated under the Life Skill

Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) is being 
implemented by Ministry of Rural Development. This programme aims to help the 
rural poor including artisans and weavers to setup enterprises at the village level in 
non-agricultural sectors. SVEP is being implemented in 19 States as on 28.02.2018.

†3015. SHRI MAHESH PODDAR: Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT 
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is no provision for assessment/examination by any outside 
agency of technical ability/skill of students who passed out from ITIs, especially It 
is of private sectors;
(b) whether complaints regarding lack of required ability and skill in students 
possessing	 passed	 out	 certificates	 from	 private	 ITIs	 and	 sale	 of	 certificates	 by	 private	
ITIs without imparting any training have also been received during last three years; 
and
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 243
(c) whether Government would consider to make provision for assessment/
examination of ability/skill of students passing out from private ITIs by some outside 
agency, if so, time by when and if not, reasons therefor?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT 
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP (SHRI ANANTKUMAR HEGDE): (a) Yes, at present 
there is no provision for assessment of examination of technical ability/skill of 
students who passed out from industrial training institutes (ITIs) including ITIs of 
private sectors by any outside agency.
(b) As on date no such complaints have been received during last three years 
regarding	 lack	 of	 required	 ability	 and	 skill	 in	 students	possessing	 passed	 out	 certificates

assessment examination of the ability/skill of students passed out from private ITIs 
by some outside agency, as Directorate General of Training (DGT) of MSDE is 
conducting fair examination at the same level for all the trainees of industrial training 
institutes (ITIs) including private ITIs on pan India basis and hence there is no need 
to make such provision.

Job loss in April-June quarter of 2017
3017. SHRI MD. NADIMUL HAQUE: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that there has been a loss of 87,000 jobs in 
April-June quarter of 2017 according to sixth round of Quarterly Employment Survey 
released by Labour Bureau in February, 2018; and
(b) what steps have been taken by Government to improve the growth rates in 
employment in view of rapidly increasing workforce, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR): (a) As per the sixth round 
of Quarterly Employment Survey (QES) released by Labour Bureau, which measures 
relative change in employment situation over successive quarters in eight sectors 
of Non-farm Industrial economy viz. Manufacturing, Construction, Trade, Transport, 
Education, Health, Accommodation and Restaurants and IT/BPO, having 10 or more 
workers, there has been an overall increase of 64,000 jobs during the April-June 
quarter of 2017. The 6th round survey data also indicates a fall in manufacturing 
sector employment to the tune of 87,000. This may be due to seasonal activities of 
manufacturing units during the monsoon period.
(b) Government has taken various steps for generating employment in the country 
like encouraging private sector of economy, fast tracking various projects involving 
substantial investment and increasing public expenditure on schemes such as Prime 
Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), Mahatma Gandhi National 
Rural Employment Gaurantee Scheme (MGNREGA), Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya 

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [22 March, 2018]   ...for the 21st March, 2018 245
Grameen Kaushalya Yojna (DDU-GKY), Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban 
Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM), Make In India, Skill India, Start-up India, Digital 
India.
Government has also decided to strategically promote labour-intensive   
manufacturing and expand employment opportunities by promoting tourism and 
agro-based industries.
A new Scheme “Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojna” has been initiated 
by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in the year 2016-17 for incentivizing 
industry for promoting employment generation. Under this scheme employers would 
be provided an incentive to enhance employment where the Government will pay the 
employer’s contribution of 8.33% Employees Pension Schemes (EPS) made to new 
employees. In Textile (apparel and made-ups) sectors, the Government in addition 
will also pay the 3.67 % EPF contribution of employers. Government has announced 
a booster package of ` 6000 crores for the textile sector which is an employment 
intensive sector.
Government has also implemented the National Career Service having a portal 
(www.ncs.gov.in) for online registration and posting of jobs-seekers and provide other 
employment related services.

Establishment of steel plants at Kadapa and Bayyaram
3019. SHRI DHARMAPURI SRINIV AS:
 SHRI T.G. VENKATESH:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the task force constituted to evaluate on the 
feasibility of steel plants at Kadapa in Andhra Pradesh and Bayyaram in Telangana 
has submitted its report to the Ministry, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether it is also a fact that both the State Governments have provided the 
necessary information to Mecon Ltd. on the establishment of steel plants, if so, the 
details thereof; and
(c) whether Government has arrived at a decision to announce the establishment 
of steel plants at Kadapa and Bayyaram at the earliest, if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI VISHNU 
DEO SAI): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. In terms of the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra 
Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Steel Authority of India Ltd. (SAIL) was to 
examine the feasibility of establishing integrated steel plants at YSR Kadapa district 
of Andhra Pradesh and at Bayyaram in Khammam district of Telangana. As per the 
feasibility report submitted by SAIL on 02.12.2014, the setting up of steel plant is 
prima	 facie	 not	 financially	 viable.	 Subsequently,	 a	 Task	 Force	 has	 been	 constituted	
on 19.10.2016 comprising of representatives from the Central and concerned State 
Governments, SAIL, RINL, NMDC Ltd., MECON Ltd. and MSTC Ltd. to suggest 
a road map for setting up of Steel Plants in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. In the 
last meeting of the Task Force held on 27.12.2017, it was decided that the concerned 
State Government would share with MECON the data for preparation of report and 
work	 out	 realistic	 assumptions.	 Based	 on	 complete	 information/confirmation	from	 both	
the State Governments, MECON would complete the Feasibility Report.

Collaboration with private sector to promote tourism
3027. SHRI HARSHV ARDHAN SINGH DUNGARPUR: Will the Minister of 
TOURISM be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government proposes to collaborate with private sector to promote 
tourism in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps being taken by Government in this regard?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF TOURISM (SHRI K. J. 
ALPHONS): (a) to (c) The Ministry of Tourism, on an ongoing and regular basis, 
holds consultations with private sector stakeholders in the tourism industry on various 
issues relating to the promotion and development of tourism in the country. The 
National Tourism Advisory Council which has been constituted to act as a ‘Think 
Tank’ to advise the Ministry on various policy matters relating to tourism, includes 
private sector stakeholders as its members.
The Ministry of Tourism has launched an ‘Adopt a Heritage Scheme’ wherein 
Private Sector Companies, Public Sector Companies and Corporate individuals can 
adopt monuments, heritage and tourist sites across India and take up the responsibility 
of operations and maintenance of certain basic and advanced tourist amenities for 
making our heritage and tourism more sustainable.

Statement
Salient features of Khelo India vertical ‘Play Field Development’ 
A	 National	 inventory	 of	 playfields	 and	 sports	 infrastructure	 will	 be	 prepared	 on	
a Geographic Information System (GIS) platform for their optimum utilisation. In 
order to put in place a strong institutionalized mechanism for preserving, protecting, 
developing	 and	 promoting	 playfields,	 State	 and	 district	 playfield	 Associations	 will	
be	 created	 in	 all	 States/UTs	 on	 the	 lines	 of	 National	 Playfield	 Association	 of	 India	
(NPFAI). District and State level Associations will register existing play areas, map 
them	 on	 the	 GIS	 platform	 and	 affiliate	 with	 the	 National	 Playing	 Fields	 Association	
(NPFAI) through district and State associations, thereby creating a National database. 
Development of playgrounds in all gram panchayats can be taken up in convergence 
with the scheme of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS) and any other scheme(s) of the State Government/Central Government. 
It	 would	 also	 include	 development	 of	 model	 playfields	 on	 pilot	 basis.
Salient features of Khelo India vertical ‘Utilisation and Creation/  
Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure’ 
Majority of the schools, colleges and even Universities lack proper play grounds 
as well as sporting infrastructure in the country. Efforts will be made to utilize 
the existing available sports infrastructure through a system of active management 
committee consisting of players and members of neighborhood community as well 
all over the country especially those under the control of Central Government/State 
Governments. A suitable mechanism will be evolved to identify gaps in availability of 
sporting	 infrastructure	 across	 the	 country	 and	 fill	these	 gaps	 with	 support	 under	 Khelo	
India. Scheme of Khelo India will also be converged with Members of Parliament  
Local Area Development (MPLAD) Scheme. The States may also provide for 
convergence of Member of Legislative Assembly Local Area Development (MLALAD) 
Scheme with Khelo India Scheme. This Component will have the following two sub 
components :
(i) University Centre of Excellence Programme: For setting up centers of sporting 
excellence in selected Universities.
(ii) Creation of Appropriate Sports Infrastructure: Under this component, grants-
in-aid will be provided to States/UTs, SAI etc. to develop critical sports 
infrastructure and other infrastructure where there are gaps.

Statement-II
Brief on the procedure adopted for the purpose as per guidelines 
framed under the vertical of
Talent Search and Development under the Khelo India Scheme.
1.	 Under	 this	 vertical,	 talent	 identification	 is	 to	 be	 done	 through	 a	 three	 tier	
structure,	 comprising	 the	 Talent	 Identification	 and	 Development	 Committee	
(TIDC) for each Sports discipline, the Talent Screening Committee (TSC), 
and the High Powered Committee (HPC). The duly constituted HPC, based 
on recommendations from various stakeholders, is to decide on sports 
disciplines to be supported under the Scheme, from time to time. Each sports 
discipline	 will	 have	 specific	 parameters	 for	 selection	 depending	 on	 its	 nature	
and the individuals to be assessed. The parameters are to be decided by the 
duly constituted HPC in consultation with the eminent sportspersons of the 
respective	 sports	 disciplines	 for	 which	 athletes	 are	 to	 be	 identified.
2. The TSC may observe players during various competitions/camps and make 
list	 of	 talented	 players.	 The	 list	 along	 with	 profile	 is	 to	 be	 put	 up	 and	
presented before TIDC for each sports. The TIDC for each sports discipline 
is	 to	 recommend	 the	 final	 list	 of	 players	 for	 talent	 support.	 Under	 normal	
circumstances, the HPC will consider the recommendations of the TIDCs 
and	 take	 final	 decision.	 However,	 owing	 to	 paucity	 of	 time	 or	 any	 other	
compelling	 reason(s),	 for	 the	 benefit	 of	 players,	 cross	 cutting	 influence	 on	
various sports or for any other reason, any matter can be directly decided 
by the HPC.
3. Brief composition of the three types of committees is given hereunder:–
(i) Talent Screening Committee (TSC), consisting of eminent athletes, coaches 
and other stake holders, as may be deemed necessary.
(ii)	 Talent	 Identification	 and	 Development	 Committee	 (TIDC)	 consisting	 of	
eminent athletes, National Observer, eminent coaches, Talent scouts, 
Sports Scientists and Representative from the National Sports Federation 
(NSF) and Director General (DG)/Deputy Director General (DDG), Sports 
Authority of India (SAI).
(iii) High Powered Committee (HPC) consisting of Secretary (Sports), 
Government of India, as Chairman, DDG, SAI as Chief Executive 
Officer	(CEO)	and	Member	Secretary,	eminent	sportspersons	(03),	eminent	
Coaches (02), representative of Indian Olympic Association (IOA) , 
representative of Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) and 
Sports Science Experts as members.
